replies.body:
Ya that's what https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/541 is doing but I think there's a few issues with it

1. Every time we add new parts, we have to extend the `"not": {"enum": ["text", "tool_call", "...", "compaction"]}` to disallow more values which is "breaking". @felixfbecker mentioned that in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/519#issuecomment-5733921144
1. I can't think of an ergonomic way to express `"not": {"enum": []}` pattern in Python or TS (I can't think of any language that can express this actually). So we'll still have the issue where util-genai allows `Any`.
  
   Another option if we really want it flat is to specify a prefix like `custom.` for `GenericPart.type` which can at least be expressed in TS as proper discriminated union (but not in python)
   ```ts
   {type: "text", text: string} | {type: `custom.{$string}`, [key: string]: unknown}
   ```

Structurally, these are more or less the same. Would something like this be better?

```json
[
  {"type": "text", "text": "hello agent"},
  {"type": "custom", "data": {"type": "foo_part", ...}}
]
```

> {"type": "custom", "data": {"type": "foo_part", ...

this means that any part needs to start within a custom type and after it's added to semconv it needs to move up one layer.  It seems unnecessary.

More importantly, this tells consumers that they have a limited set of types they should expect. This is not right - they should expect parts with any types.

> Every time we add new parts, we have to extend the "not": {"enum": ["text", "tool_call", "...", "compaction"]} to disallow more values which is "breaking"

why is it breaking? It only changes what deserializes to GenericPart vs specific future part, it does not make anything invalid. GenericPart is not a thing to be used on its own.

> I can't think of an ergonomic way to express "not": {"enum": []} pattern in Python or TS

Custom deserializer that would look at discriminator and then deserialize object to corresponding part can be written. Also, we don't ever need to record GenericPart on the producer side. Only consumers need to be able to deserialize it and they should be able to write custom deserializer that keeps it a dics, drops, or try to interpret custom parts.

In any case, my main concern is that json schema should tell consumers what to expect and the answer is they should expect unknown discriminator values. They can come from custom parts or from future semconv parts.

> this means that any part needs to start within a custom type and after it's added to semconv it needs to move up one layer. It seems unnecessary.

Ya it's by design in this PR. I think it's impossible that when new part types get codified in semconv, the existing producers' custom part structure will match exactly. The idea is to keep custom and semconv fields separate to avoid any collision between custom parts and semconv defined parts.

> In any case, my main concern is that json schema should tell consumers what to expect and the answer is they should expect unknown discriminator values. They can come from custom parts or from future semconv parts.

👍 

---

A proposal which keeps things flat but still keeps custom parts separate:

1. Update `GenericPart` to use the not-enum pattern you showed above which will make it work for outdated consumers deserializing a "future added value" from the official semconv.
2. Add a `CustomPart` to the `oneOf` that requires `type` to have vendor/custom prefixing like `anthropic.foo` (via regex pattern), and it has additionalProperties allowed (flatly).

Then, we can update util-genai in python/TS removing GenericPart (since it's only in the schema for consumers) and adding CustomPart instead (enforcing vendoring in `type`)

WDYT?
Prototyped here with updated golden tests to hopefully illustrate https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/compare/main...aabmass:semantic-conventions-genai:push-xlxyuuuqqwkr

Let's do just p1 (not-enum on `GenericPart`) in this PR and drop `CustomPart` ?

CustomPart doesn't fix anything the not-enum fallback doesn't already cover. If you're concerned about name collisions, let's RECOMMEND vendors to prefix their top-level part type literals with the corresponding `gen_ai.provider.name`, for example `anthropic.search_result`.

replies.body: Any strong argument for underscores vs dots? We usually use dots in OTel

Only because I used the prefix for properties too (e.g. `anthropic_mcp_server_name`) and I thought dots are difficult for some languages to parse in field names and I wanted to stay consistent between the discriminator and field names

Discussed on the call but

- the schema description here only recommends prefixing but doesn't mandate `.` over `_` (`anthropic.search_result` is just an example, and `anthropic_search_result` is valid under the schema too)
- since `type` is a JSON string value rather than a property key, `.` shouldn't run into field-name parsing issues, and properties on the part itself don't need prefixing.

`SystemInstructionPart` reuses this `GenericPart`, so system instructions now reject every message part type too (`blob`, `uri`, `file`, ...) - neither as a known part nor as a generic one. If semconv later adds e.g. `blob` to system instructions, consumers on the current schema will fail to validate it, which is the forward-compat case this fallback is meant to cover. Should the system instructions fallback exclude only the types defined there?

```python
class GenericSystemInstructionPart(GenericPart):
    type: str = Field(
        description=GenericPart.model_fields["type"].description,
        json_schema_extra=_not_known_types(TextPart),
    )


SystemInstructionPart = Union[
    TextPart,
    GenericSystemInstructionPart,
]
```
